comparator.name: Slavonic Language and Culture
comparator.sourceNotes: The retained Russian main-language major remains a valid ordinary pathway independent of UCR fit. The adopted 2026–2027 OER Appendix 1 and dated course list give 60 EC per year. Riga at the University of Latvia is the required Russian-route second-year destination, with a 54 first-year plus 18 second-year EC gate including Russian 5 and 6. The exchange follows prescribed subject lines and nonduplication rules, unlike the separate genuinely open thirty-credit third-year group. The Slavic research lab follows the completed advanced aspect/literature/language units and precedes the individual twelve-credit thesis. Writing diagnostic and tutoring carry no credits. Programme instruction is Dutch with target-language work and some English course instruction; no invented numeric thesis threshold or word count is imported.
components: Russian and Eastern European Cultural History
A Dutch writing diagnostic and recurring tutoring accompany the programme. They carry no credits.
The Human World: Introduction to the Humanities
A World of Regions: Introduction to Area Studies
Complete A World of Regions and Russian 3 before this course, which includes historical Slavic phonology, morphology and older texts.
This example follows Russian. Polish, Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian and Czech are alternative main-language choices.
Complete Russian 1 and 2 before Russian 3; Russian 4 follows Russian 3. Russian 5 requires Russian 4, and Russian 6 requires Russian 5.
Philosophy of Science: National Identity, Borders and Territoriality
Russian & East European Literatures: The Classics
Complete the first year before Language Contact. Russian 5 and 6 and The History of Slavic provide recommended preparation.
Study Abroad in Slavonic Languages and Cultures

The Russian pathway requires the second semester of year two at the University of Latvia in Riga. Before departure, pass at least 54 first-year EC and 18 EC from the first semester of year two, including Russian 5 and 6. The 30 EC must follow the programme’s cultural-history, linguistics/translation, literature or language-acquisition lines without duplicating home study. Language courses must exceed the stated B1 speaking/writing and B2 reading exit levels. Students unable to travel for valid reasons need Examination Board approval for a 30-EC home alternative.
Making Sense of Aspect in Time and Space
This course requires level-three Slavic language acquisition or equivalent. The completed Russian sequence supplies the preparation.
Russian and Eastern European Literature after 1950

Pass Russian 6, Making Sense of Aspect in Time and Space and Russian and Eastern European Literature after 1950 before the lab. It develops qualitative and quantitative language/literature research and a thesis proposal.

Thirty credits remain available for electives, a minor or an optional placement. Normally no more than 12 EC may be introductory; an approved UvA minor or one-language sequence can permit up to 24 EC. External study requires Examination Board approval, minors cannot duplicate compulsory language study, and placements occupy at most 12 EC.
Bachelor’s Thesis in Slavonic Languages and Cultures

The twelve-credit thesis is a supervised individual research project using critically evaluated primary and secondary sources. The research lab prepares its proposal. It is normally written in Dutch; a different language requires Examination Board approval. Register for the thesis and follow the programme handbook’s supervision and submission rules.

routeSelection.basis: The existing Russian main-language major is still a complete current published option. Retained independently of UCR fit, rather than reopening a sound route merely because catalogue list order differs from the public list. Its prescribed destination is Riga; no other language branch or destination is stacked.

exception.reason: UCR offers substantial literary interpretation, language-processing research, cultural and historical analysis, European institutions and social inquiry. These provide real related study, including Soviet documentary history, but do not combine into sustained investigation of Slavic languages, literature and Central or Eastern European societies. Expanding these methods across a complete programme changes the focus to general humanities or European social science. The conclusion concerns the programme’s academic substance, not language acquisition alone or a professional qualification.

exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Three complete 24-course internal trials pass current offering, prerequisite and numerical checks. Screened all 151 current identities and read plausible language, literary, historical, art/media, social and political contributions. Psycholinguistics and stylistics receive substantive language-science weight; literary interpretation, Soviet documentary history, empire, conflict, identity and European institutions provide actual related content. Their combination does not sustain Slavic historical linguistics, regional literary and cultural history or contemporary regional inquiry. The excluded historical Walcheren outline is not used. Description-only courses receive the full scope their descriptions support.

candidateAssessment.concept: Slavic language, linguistics and language-mediated culture
candidateAssessment.assessment: A full trial combines psycholinguistics, stylistic/grammatical analysis, literature, rhetoric, media, historical and qualitative/social methods. This supplies substantial language-and-culture inquiry but not Slavic historical morphology, aspect, source-language literature and region-specific cultural research. Missing language acquisition alone is not the no-match criterion.

candidateAssessment.concept: Eastern European literature, cultural history and intellectual life
candidateAssessment.assessment: A full trial tests the complete literature sequence, life writing, adaptation, cultural theory, art/heritage, film/documentary and historical research. Soviet documentary cinema is a genuine regional connection and is not ignored. It does not extend into sustained Russian, Polish, Czech or Balkan literary, intellectual and cultural history; the larger programme becomes general cultural humanities.

candidateAssessment.concept: Russian and Eastern European history, politics, society and conflict
candidateAssessment.assessment: A full trial tests modern and imperial history, European institutions, comparative politics, international relations, conflict, sociology, qualitative inquiry and public policy/economics. These offer concrete analysis of institutions, power and change. They do not accumulate into sustained study of Eastern European histories, post-Soviet societies, Balkan conflicts or region-specific sources; the resulting programme becomes broader European/global social science.
